title: Polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)
summary: In autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, many fluid-filled sacs (cysts) grow in the kidneys over time. It often causes high blood pressure, and kidney function may slowly fall in adulthood.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal dominant way: one changed copy of one of the genes linked to it (PKD1 or PKD2) can be enough to cause it. A parent with the change can pass it on, and the chance is the same for each pregnancy. A genetic counsellor talks this through with you.
carrier_meaning: For a dominant condition, one changed copy can be enough to cause it, so people with a change are not usually called carriers. How much it affects someone varies, and some people have few signs for many years. A genetic counsellor explains what a result means.
disease_meaning: How it affects someone varies a lot. Kidney specialists check blood pressure and kidney function regularly, and treatments can slow it down. There is also a rarer recessive form that starts in childhood; a counsellor can explain the difference.
screening: A genetic test can look for a change in one of the genes linked to it (PKD1 or PKD2). Testing is a personal choice, and counselling before and after the test is part of it.

card_summary: Cysts grow in the kidneys over time, usually in adulthood.

disease_short: Kidney cysts grow over time; kidney specialists check and treat it.
care: Kidney clinics, blood pressure care, genetic counselling and family support groups.
